chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad informed me, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-ʿAbbās, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"There is no objection to wiping the feet, forward and backward."

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: Wudu (ablution) is an act of nearness to Allah, so it befits the servant to make the intention sincere in it and to make it for the sake of Allah, the Exalted.
That which indicates the obligation of intention is His saying, Exalted is He: "O you who believe! When you rise for salat (prayer), wash your faces"—the verse.

His saying, "wash," means: wash for salat (prayer). The mention of salat was only omitted for brevity, and the usage of the Arabs in that is clear; for when they say, "When you intend to meet the ruler, then wear your clothes," and, "When you intend to meet the enemy, then take your weapon," the understood sense of the speech is: wear your clothes for meeting the ruler, and take your weapon for meeting the enemy. So when we are commanded to wash for salat (prayer), intention is indispensable, because through intention the act is directed to salat (prayer) rather than to anything else; and this also indicates the obligation of intention.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the act for which the washing is performed
key_terms.النِّيَّةِ: intention, by which the act is directed toward worship
key_terms.الْقَدَمَيْنِ: the two feet, the limbs referred to in the ruling of wiping
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification discussed in the passage
key_terms.فَاغْسِلُوا: wash, the Qur'anic imperative cited as evidence
key_terms.قُرْبَةٌ: an act of drawing near to Allah
key_terms.مَسْحِ: wiping, specifically the act of wiping the feet in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.وُجُوبِ: obligation, the legal necessity being argued for

ai.seo_question: Does wudu (ablution) require niyyah (intention), and is it permissible to wipe the feet forward and backward?
ai.summary: This passage contains a hadith from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام permitting wiping the feet in either direction during wudu (ablution). It then presents al-Shaykh's explanation that wudu (ablution) is an act of قربَة to Allah and therefore requires sincere niyyah (intention), supported by a linguistic reading of the Qur'anic command regarding purification for salat (prayer).
